subject: chemistry
title: Counting Atoms in Formulae
welcome_lead: Subscripts, brackets and big numbers: learn to count atoms like a chemist.
meta_desc: Practise counting atoms in chemical formulae in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now count atoms in any common chemical formula.

concepts.def: Symbols and numbers showing the atoms in a substance.
Small number after a symbol; counts atoms of that element.
Big number in front; multiplies all atoms in the formula.
Group atoms; multiplied by the subscript outside.
2H₂O means 2 water molecules: 4 H and 2 O atoms total.
Sum all atoms once subscripts and coefficients are applied.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The little number AFTER a symbol counts atoms of that element only.

H₂O: 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen = 3 atoms.
CO₂: 1 carbon + 2 oxygen = 3 atoms.

A big number BEFORE a formula multiplies everything in it.

2H₂O = 2 × (2H + 1O) = 4 H + 2 O = 6 atoms total.

Brackets group atoms together. The subscript outside multiplies everything inside.

Ca(OH)₂: 1 calcium + 2 oxygen + 2 hydrogen = 5 atoms.

Practice makes perfect!
